html:
The Hikayat Hang Tuah is a long Malay prose epic about Hang Tuah, a legendary warrior and admiral of the Malacca Sultanate. It was written down in the 17th or 18th century.

Hang Tuah serves his sultan with total loyalty, even when wrongly ordered to be killed. His friend Hang Jebat rebels to avenge him, and Hang Tuah kills Jebat. The tale of the duel has been argued over ever since: is loyalty or justice the higher virtue?

The epic gave the Malay world its most famous hero and the saying that Malays will never vanish from the earth. Like the Malay Annals, it is a core text of Malay literature. See also Malay language.
